questions.statement: What is the primary objective of High-Level Design (HLD)?
options: Designing the system architecture to meet scalability, reliability, and other requirements

questions.statement: Which of the following is an example of vertical scaling?
options: Increasing the RAM and CPU of an existing server

questions.statement: What is a major advantage of horizontal scaling?
options: It allows capacity to increase by adding more machines

questions.statement: What is a disadvantage of vertical scaling?
options: It has hardware limits and may create a single point of failure

questions.statement: In Back-of-the-Envelope Estimation, what does QPS represent?
A service receives 8,640,000 requests per day. What is its approximate average QPS?
What does SPOF stand for?
Which availability level permits approximately 52.6 minutes of downtime per year?
What is the primary purpose of DNS?
options: Converting domain names into IP addresses

questions.statement: Which component typically provides the final IP address for a domain during DNS resolution?
Which sequence correctly represents the TCP three-way handshake?
Which protocol is connection-oriented and provides reliable, ordered delivery?
Which is a suitable use case for UDP?
In a typical scalable web architecture, why are backend servers placed in private subnets?
options: To make them directly accessible to everyone
To prevent direct public access and reduce exposure
To eliminate the need for authentication

questions.statement: What is the primary purpose of a load balancer?
options: To distribute incoming traffic across backend servers

questions.statement: Which load-balancing algorithm distributes requests sequentially among servers?
Which algorithm considers the number of active connections on each server?
What is a key characteristic of an L7 load balancer?
options: It operates exclusively at the physical layer
It can route based on HTTP paths, headers, or cookies

questions.statement: Which is an example of an L4 load balancer?
What is the purpose of a load balancer health check?
options: To identify unhealthy backend servers and stop routing traffic to them

questions.statement: What is a major drawback of sticky sessions?
options: They create dependency on a particular server and complicate failover and scaling

questions.statement: In a primary-replica database architecture, which node typically handles writes?
What is replication lag?
options: Delay between a write on the primary and its visibility on a replica
Delay in creating a load balancer

questions.statement: Which replication mode generally provides stronger durability and consistency guarantees but may increase write latency?
What is database sharding?
options: Duplicating the same data on every server
Horizontally partitioning data across multiple database nodes
Moving all data to a CDN

questions.statement: In the formula Hash(UserID) % N, what does N generally represent?
options: Number of database nodes or shards

questions.statement: What is a major challenge of choosing a poor shard key?
options: It can create hot shards and uneven load distribution
It eliminates the need for indexes

questions.statement: Which statement best describes replication versus sharding?
options: Replication partitions data; sharding duplicates it
Replication duplicates data; sharding partitions data
Both always perform exactly the same function

questions.statement: Why are cross-shard JOINs problematic?
options: They may require communication across multiple nodes, increasing latency and complexity
They are faster than local queries in every case

questions.statement: What is the primary purpose of database failover?
options: To promote a healthy replica or alternate node when the primary fails
To move data to the client

questions.statement: What is the major problem with simple modulo hashing when the number of servers changes?
options: It causes many keys to map to different servers, requiring significant remapping

questions.statement: In consistent hashing, where are keys and servers mapped?
What is the main benefit of consistent hashing?
options: It minimizes key remapping when nodes are added or removed
It eliminates the need for caching

questions.statement: What is the purpose of virtual nodes in consistent hashing?
options: To improve key distribution and reduce load imbalance across physical nodes

questions.statement: Which caching strategy fetches data from the database only after a cache miss and then populates the cache?
Which caching strategy writes to the cache first and persists to the database asynchronously?
Which eviction policy removes the least recently accessed items?
What is the difference between TTL and an eviction policy?
options: TTL determines when a key expires; eviction policy determines what to remove when space is needed
TTL is only used for databases

questions.statement: According to the CAP theorem, during a network partition, a distributed system must trade off between:
Which statement best describes eventual consistency?
options: Every read always immediately returns the latest write
Replicas may temporarily differ but converge if no new updates occur

questions.statement: Which messaging pattern ensures that a message is processed by one consumer within a consumer group?
In Kafka, what is a partition?
options: An ordered, append-only sequence of messages within a topic

questions.statement: In Kafka, what is the role of a consumer group?
options: It ensures every consumer receives every message in the group
It allows consumers to divide partitions for parallel processing

questions.statement: If a Kafka topic has 3 partitions and a consumer group has 5 consumers, how many consumers can actively consume partitions at the same time?
What is a Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) used for?
options: Holding messages that repeatedly fail processing for later inspection

questions.statement: Which is a key advantage of asynchronous processing using a message queue?
options: It forces all services to remain tightly coupled
It decouples producers and consumers and can absorb temporary traffic spikes
It guarantees zero message loss in every configuration
It eliminates the need for monitoring

questions.statement: Which statement best describes the Saga pattern?
options: It provides a traditional ACID rollback across all independent databases
It coordinates a distributed business transaction using local transactions and compensating actions
It is a caching eviction policy
It is a TCP handshake mechanism

questions.statement: What is the main idea of CQRS?
options: Separating command or write responsibilities from query or read responsibilities

questions.statement: Why are access tokens generally short-lived while refresh tokens are longer-lived?
options: Access tokens are used frequently and should limit the damage if compromised; refresh tokens obtain new access tokens
Refresh tokens are always sent with every API request
Access tokens are used only for database backups
